title: The one-hour workspace reset
subtitle: A practical checklist for turning a cluttered desk and scattered tasks into a usable work session.
audience: An individual preparing a home or office workspace. Sample content only.
purpose: Finish with a clear work surface, one written priority and a repeatable five-minute closing routine. This is a local product-builder demonstration, not a commercial offer.

sections.heading: Choose a useful finish line (5 minutes)
sections.summary: Decide what a better workspace means today before rearranging everything.

items.label: Name the next real task
items.detail: Write one concrete result you want to produce after the reset, such as a first draft or a reviewed checklist. Keep this note visible.

items.label: Set a small boundary
items.detail: Choose one desk or work surface. Leave shared spaces and other people's belongings alone unless they have agreed.

items.label: Prepare three temporary places
items.detail: Use simple labels: keep here, move elsewhere, and review later. Do not discard important documents or anything you are unsure about.

sections.heading: Make the physical space usable (20 minutes)
sections.summary: Aim for enough clear space to work comfortably, not a perfect-looking room.

items.label: Remove only obvious distractions
items.detail: Move unrelated loose objects into the temporary places. Keep the tools needed for your chosen task within reach.

items.label: Check the working position
items.detail: Make room for your hands and materials, reduce visible glare where practical, and move loose cables away from paths. Do not open or repair electrical equipment.

items.label: Resolve the easy items
items.detail: Return familiar objects to their known places. Put uncertain items in the review-later group and write a time to revisit them.

sections.heading: Reduce digital friction (20 minutes)
sections.summary: Use reversible changes and keep originals intact.

items.label: Save work before closing anything
items.detail: Save open drafts and record browser tabs you need later. Do not delete files, reset settings or change another person's shared workspace.

items.label: Gather the next task's references
items.detail: Create a short list of the files and links you need. Check that you can open them. Leave passwords and private customer data out of the list.

items.label: Choose one capture place
items.detail: Use an existing note or notebook for incoming tasks during the work session. A new app or subscription is not required.

sections.heading: Start and keep the reset (15 minutes)
sections.summary: A useful reset makes the next action easier and creates a small closing habit.

items.label: Do a five-minute test
items.detail: Begin the real task named in section one. Note any missing tool, reference or obstacle you encounter, and fix the smallest reversible issue.

items.label: Write the next action
items.detail: Record the next visible step and the file or place where work will continue. Keep it specific enough to resume without reconstructing your plan.

items.label: Set a five-minute close
items.detail: At the end of your next work session, save the work, put tools back and write tomorrow's first action. Review this checklist after three sessions and adjust it.
